daily.title: Baghdad confirms attack on Saudi pipeline came from Iraq
daily.summary: Saudi Arabia has said it will not relatiate and wants Iraq to "take the necessary measures." Baghdad is under pressure from the United States to rein in Iran-backed militias.

daily.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
daily.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

daily.title: Ukraine: Several killed in series of Russian strikes
daily.summary: Local authorities said several civilians were killed and dozens more wounded across Ukraine by Russian strikes. Meanwhile, the Kremlin has rejected Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal to meet with the Russian leader in Miami.

daily.title: Bulgaria: Fire at factory making munitions for Ukraine
daily.summary: Bulgarian authorities are investigating a fire at a munitions factory for links to an explosion at a similar facility in August. Arms maker EMCO says no human error was involved, as investigators look at sabotage.

daily.title: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
daily.summary: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.

daily.title: Uganda lays 'boy king' Oyo to rest amid succession row
daily.summary: Uganda has buried King Oyo Nyimba, who was crowned in the Tooro Kingdom in 1995 aged just 3. His death at 34 has triggered a dispute over a successor, as rumors abound of possible heirs born out of wedlock.

daily.title: BRICS summit leaders urge 'maximum restraint' in Middle East
daily.summary: The joint declaration at the BRICS 2026 summit expressed 'deep concern' over hostilities in the Middle East. China's President Xi Jinping said the Iran war was not in the bloc's interest.

daily.title: Russian GRU spies behind failed Leipzig attack: reports
daily.summary: A German newspaper has cited reports tying a failed attack at Leipzig Airport to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency. One suspect's ties to GRU were known when he entered the country, yet he was not surveilled.

daily.title: Brazil: Flavio Bolsonaro faces corruption probe weeks before election
daily.summary: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, Lula's top rival in next month's election, is under investigation for alleged corruption linked to financing a biopic about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

daily.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Ninos intensifying?
daily.summary: Records from the past few decades show that, during this period, El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme. But is this normal, or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

daily.title: Uber leaves two key African markets — and their drivers in despair
daily.summary: Uber's departure from Nigeria and Uganda has left countless customers high and dry. But what about drivers? With fuel prices, maintenance, and other operating costs rising, many say they're struggling to make a living.

daily.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles day after trilateral drills end
daily.summary: North Korea launched several short-range ballistic missiles into the sea a day after the US, South Korea and Japan concluded joint military exercises Pyongyang had called provocative.

daily.title: Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
daily.summary: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

daily.title: DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
daily.summary: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

daily.title: France: Sabotage suspected in train derailment
daily.summary: Dozens were injured when a train derailed between Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwest France, on Friday evening. Police believe the accident may have been deliberately caused, local media say.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russian strike on Kyiv gas station kills 2
weekly.summary: With fighting on the front lines mostly stalled, Russia has been increasingly hitting petrol stations and other civilian targets. Ukraine has also been attacking Russia with drones, killing three people on Friday.

weekly.title: US commemorates 25 years since 9/11 terror attack
weekly.summary: A quarter century has passed since Islamists hijacked four commercial jets and turned them into weapons against the US. On Friday, ceremonies in New York, Pennsylvania and Washington DC marked the dark anniversary.

weekly.title: Iran pursues cautious escalation ahead of US midterms
weekly.summary: Tehran appears to be boosting pressure on Washington ahead of the crucial midterm vote, but shows little desire to return to a full-scale war.

weekly.title: India's BRICS strategy tested with Xi, Putin set to visit
weekly.summary: New Delhi's "America Plus" approach sees India deepening its ties with China and Russia, while also trying to keep BRICS from turning into an anti-Western platform.

weekly.title: Iran war: Saudi-Houthi escalation intensifies Yemen conflict
weekly.summary: The Houthi takeovers of Mokha, Dhubab and Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait threaten to push Yemen deeper into the Middle East war. The Iran-backed group has made advances against Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia.

weekly.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
weekly.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

weekly.title: Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

weekly.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
weekly.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

weekly.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

weekly.title: Germany sets its sights on Russia's shadow fleet
weekly.summary: The German government wants to follow other EU countries and take more decisive action against Russia's shadow fleet, accusing it of helping Moscow evade sanctions and carry out acts of sabotage.

weekly.title: Cyberattack in Berlin: 1.4 million files on the dark web
weekly.summary: Shortly before Berlin's state parliamentary election, the hacker group Rhysida stole data, tried to extort the Berlin Senate and published the data on the dark web after their attempt failed.

weekly.title: Germany’s Goethe-Institut is closing in Russia. Russians tell DW how canceled exams are upending their plans
weekly.summary: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia affects their lives.

weekly.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
weekly.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

weekly.title: Are electric cars really bad for the environment?
weekly.summary: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

weekly.title: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
weekly.summary: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

weekly.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
weekly.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

weekly.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
weekly.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

weekly.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?
weekly.summary: Six months after Saudi Arabia pulled funding from the breakaway organization, LIV Golf have filed for bankruptcy protection. Several of the world's best players signed on to LIV, so where does that leave golf?

weekly.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
weekly.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

weekly.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
weekly.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

weekly.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
weekly.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

weekly.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
weekly.summary: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."

weekly.title: Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
weekly.summary: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

weekly.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
weekly.summary: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

weekly.title: Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
weekly.summary: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

weekly.title: BSW and AfD – a political love-hate relationship in Germany
weekly.summary: The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) could help the Alternative for Germany (AfD) into power in Saxony-Anhalt. But the BSW is riddled with infighting

weekly.title: Afghanistan's women: A national soccer team without a home
weekly.summary: The Afghan women's national football team has finally been officially recognized by FIFA. Now the players want to make history both on and off the field.

weekly.title: PISA 2025 results: Reading and math scores plummet worldwide
weekly.summary: The PISA 2025 results reveal record-low student performance, with digital distractions and AI use raising concerns. Germany is faring worse than ever.

weekly.title: Elversberg: Bundesliga newcomers from tiny town make waves
weekly.summary: A team from a small southwestern German town of just 7,000 inhabitants made history by sealing promotion to become the 59th club to play in the Bundesliga. Elversberg has got off to a memorable start.

weekly.title: Egg freezing in women's football: Choice or pressure?
weekly.summary: Spain's football federation is set to join a handful of clubs in paying for female players to freeze their eggs. Experts have welfare concerns.

weekly.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back
weekly.summary: As his latest movie, "Bucking Fastard," premiered at the Venice Film Festival, DW talked to the boundary-breaking director.

weekly.title: Nicaragua challenges German arms exports to Israel at ICJ
weekly.summary: Germany has asked the International Court of Justice to dismiss the case on jurisdiction grounds. It also said its arms exports to Israel were documented, published, and subject to more stringent checks than most.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Germany wakes up to 'unsettling' AfD victory
weekly.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the Saxony-Anhalt state election but without an absolute majority in parliament. Other European nations were wrestling with the impact of the results. Follow DW.

weekly.title: AfD wants to form a government in Saxony-Anhalt — but how?
weekly.summary: Following its record election success, the far-right Alternative for Germany aims to form a government. What options does it have without the absolute majority?

weekly.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
weekly.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

weekly.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
weekly.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

weekly.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
weekly.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Digesting the AfD's landmark election win
weekly.summary: With well over 40% for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), Saxony-Anhalt has witnessed a landmark election night. DW's reporters were on the ground.

weekly.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: False and misleading claims are raising questions about the integrity of the election in Saxony-Anhalt. DW Fact Check takes a closer look.

weekly.title: Germany set to feel the impact of Saxony-Anhalt's AfD win
weekly.summary: The state election could have major consequences for Germany's government. Pollsters cite dissatisfaction with Merz as one reason for the CDU's poor showing.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
weekly.summary: The AfD has emerged as the strongest party in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt by a wide margin. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

weekly.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
weekly.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

weekly.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
weekly.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

weekly.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
weekly.summary: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.
